rows.Finding description: Surface biotinylation and ELISA showed a 53% lower APOER2 surface-to-total ratio in APOE4 than APOE3 mouse neurons across three cohorts.
rows.Finding quote: The results obtained show that the ratio of the externally oriented receptors to the total, was significantly lower in APOE4 neurons of APOER2 (Fig. 4A, 53% reduction, p < 0.05) and LRP1 (Fig. 4B, 48.03% reduction, p < 0.05) than those of the corresponding APOE3 cells.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower neuronal APOER2 surface-to-total ratio)
rows.Experimental system: Brain-derived neuron-enriched primary cultures from 1–3-day-old human-APOE3/4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; DIV21; surface biotinylation at 4°C and receptor ELISA; three pooled-pup cohorts.

rows.Finding description: The APOER2 fraction colocalizing with early endosomes increased from 0.37 in APOE3 to 0.50 in APOE4 neurons, with 20 and 31 cells respectively from three preparations. Effect is the ratio of the two group values printed in the quote (0.50±0.03 and 0.37±0.04).
rows.Finding quote: Similar analysis of the effect of the APOE genotype on the colocalization of APOER2 with the early endosomes revealed an opposite effect to that seen with LRP1; Accordingly, more APOER2 is localized in the early endosomes in APOE4 cells as indicated by the M1 colocalization variable described in the material and methods section (0.50±0.03, N = 31 from 3 different preparations) than in the APOE3 cells (0.37±0.04, N = 20 from 3 different preparations) neurons (p < 0.05).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher fraction of APOER2 colocalizing with early endosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Brain-derived neuron-enriched primary cultures from 1–3-day-old human-APOE3/4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; DIV21; APOER2/Rab5 double staining, confocal microscopy and M1 colocalization.

rows.Finding description: APOER2 early-endosomal colocalization increased from 0.37 in APOE3 to 0.51 in APOE4 neurons, measured in 25–37 cells from two to three preparations.
rows.Finding quote: A different colocalization pattern was seen in APOER2, IR, and VEGFR, where the accumulation of these receptors in the early endosomes in APOE4 neurons (see also Figs. 5 and 6) is accompanied with lower levels of colocalization in late endosomes relative to those obtained with APOE3 cells.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher fraction of APOER2 colocalizing with early endosomes)

rows.Finding description: APOER2 recycling-endosomal colocalization showed no significant difference between genotypes, despite a reported 11.16% decrease in APOE4 neurons; 25–37 cells from two to three preparations were analyzed.
rows.Finding quote: Additionally, there was also a decrease in the colocalization of the receptors with the lysosomes in APOE4 neurons that was significant in APOER2 and VEGFR but not in the IR (APOER2 : 35.89% decrease, p < 0.0001; VEGFR: 31.30% decrease, p < 0.05), and in the recycling endosomes in all three receptors (APOER2 : 11.16% decrease, p = 0.5154; IR: 30.88% decrease, p < 0.05; VEGFR: 29.02% decrease, p < 0.05) when compared to APOE3 neurons.

rows.Finding description: LRP1 knockdown reduced APOER2 early-endosomal colocalization in APOE4 neurons by a reported 38.8%, assessed in 50–53 cells from five preparations.
rows.Finding quote: As can be seen, the downregulation of LRP1 had no significant effects on the total levels of the receptors, had no effect on the size of early endosomes (not shown), but did abolish the excess colocalization of these receptors with early endosomes in APOE4 neurons (the percent of reduction when compared to APOE4 control equals to 38.8% in APOER2, 48.9% in IR, and 64.1% in VEGFR).
rows.Finding summary: (LRP1 knockdown in APOE4 neurons) -> (lower fraction of APOER2 colocalizing with early endosomes)
rows.Experimental system: Brain-derived primary neurons from neonatal human-APOE4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-synuclein-null background; AAV9 LRP1 gRNA plus Cas9 at DIV3; collection ten days later per CRISPR methods; APOER2/Rab5 confocal M1 analysis in transduced cells.
rows.Data location: Fig. 12B, APOER2, APOE4-LRP1 AAv versus APOE4 control

rows.Finding description: Both lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4 reduced surface LDLR relative to ApoE2 in APOE-knockout human iPSC-derived astrocytes, without an established additional ApoE4 effect.
rows.Finding quote: In H4, WT HAP1, and APOE KO iAstrocytes, incubation with lipApoE3/E4 significantly reduced surface LDLR relative to lipApoE2, revealing impaired LDLR recycling accompanying increased LDLR-mediated lipApoE uptake (Figure 2A–D, Figure S2A–B).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (shared astrocyte surface-LDLR depletion; E4-specific additional impairment unresolved)
rows.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes differentiated from an APOE-knockout clone of ThermoFisher A18945, originally APOE3/3; exogenous POPC-lipidated ApoE at 10 μg/mL for one day; surface LDLR immunostaining.

rows.Finding description: Quantification showed surface LDLR depletion with both ApoE3 and ApoE4 in human iPSC-derived astrocytes; the supplied text does not establish greater depletion with ApoE4.
rows.Finding quote: While all 3 ApoE isoforms impacted LDLR mRNA levels, lipApoE3/E4 abrogated the expected increase in surface LDLR by impairing its recycling.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (shared astrocyte surface-LDLR depletion; E4-specific additional impairment unresolved)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE-knockout iPSC-derived astrocytes from ThermoFisher A18945; 10 μg/mL exogenous POPC-lipidated ApoE for one day; quantified surface LDLR immunostaining.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent HTRF experiments, lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4 had comparable high-affinity LDLR binding, both with EC50 approximately 13 nM; no significant difference is reported.
rows.Finding quote: Conversely, lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 both exhibited high affinity binding, demonstrating a half maximum effective concentration (EC50) of ~13 nM.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in reported LDLR-binding EC50)
rows.Experimental system: Cell-free HTRF using HEK293-derived, His-tagged POPC-lipidated ApoE and biotinylated human LDLR extracellular domain; pH 7.5; 1 h at room temperature; three independent titrations performed in triplicate.

rows.Finding description: SPR yielded LDLR-binding KD values of 9 nM for ApoE4 and 16 nM for ApoE3, a nominally lower ApoE4 KD that the authors characterize as comparable affinity without reporting statistical significance.
rows.Finding quote: SPR similarly revealed a high affinity LDLR binding for both lipApoE4 and lipApoE3 (KD = 9 nM and 16 nM, respectively), whereas the lipApoE2-LDLR affinity was ~50-fold lower than lipApoE3 (KD = 800 nM; Figure 1D).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (nominally lower LDLR-binding KD within author-described comparable affinities)
rows.Experimental system: Cell-free Biacore SPR with biotinylated human LDLR extracellular domain immobilized on a neutravidin-coated C1 chip; HEK293-derived POPC-lipidated ApoE3/E4 at 0.0156, 0.03125 and 0.0625 μM; 60 s association and 300 s final dissociation; 1:1 kinetic fit.

rows.Finding description: Internalized ApoE3 and ApoE4 both completely colocalized with endogenous LDLR in astrocytes, with Mander’s coefficients of 1 for each; no significant difference is reported.
rows.Finding quote: Super-resolution imaging on APOE KO iAstrocytes confirmed internalized lipApoE completely colocalized with endogenous LDLR (Mander’s coefficient for ApoE puncta with colocalizing LDLR = 1 for all 3 isoforms), largely inside LAMP1 compartments (Figure 2H) (Mander’s coefficients for ApoE puncta with colocalizing LAMP1 = 0.823 ± 0.061 for ApoE2; 0.903 ± 0.024 for ApoE3; 0.900 ± 0.008 for ApoE4).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in complete intracellular ApoE–LDLR colocalization)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE-knockout iPSC-derived astrocytes from ThermoFisher A18945; 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE for one day; super-resolution confocal co-immunostaining of ApoE, endogenous LDLR and LAMP1; Mander’s overlap analysis.

rows.Finding description: ApoE3 and ApoE4 treatment both produced modest reductions and a more clustered appearance of total LDLR in H4 cells, without a reported E4-specific difference.
rows.Finding quote: Immunostaining of total LDLR (cell surface + intracellular) in H4 cells after lipApoE3/E4 treatment showed a modest but significant reduction in signals, which also appeared slightly more clustered (Figure 2E–F).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (shared reduction and clustering of total LDLR; additional E4 effect unresolved)
rows.Experimental system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells; 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE for one day; fixed, permeabilized immunostaining of surface plus intracellular LDLR.

rows.Finding description: One-day pretreatment with either lipidated ApoE3 or ApoE4 nearly abolished subsequent LDL uptake, consistent with impaired surface-LDLR availability but without an established extra ApoE4 effect.
rows.Finding quote: When DiI-LDL was spiked into media after 1d pre-treatment with lipApoE3/E4, DiI-LDL uptake was nearly abolished (Figure 2K, L).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (shared near-abolition of subsequent LDL uptake)
rows.Experimental system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells; 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE for one day, followed by 10 μg/mL DiI-LDL for 3–4 h; live confocal imaging.

rows.Finding description: Lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4 both showed robust binding to surface LDLR; the supplied text does not establish stronger ApoE4 binding.
rows.Finding quote: Robust cell surface signals were observed for lipApoE3 and lipApoE4, while minimal signals were observed for lipApoE2, indicating reduced binding of lipApoE2 to LDLR (Figure 1A–B).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (robust LDLR surface binding with no reported E4-specific increase)
rows.Experimental system: Human HEK293T cells overexpressing human LDLR; HEK293-derived, FITC-labeled lipidated ApoE at 10 μg/mL; 1 h at 4°C to prevent endocytosis; confocal surface-binding assay.

rows.Finding description: Astrocytes accumulated more ApoE4 than ApoE3. The reported overlap coefficients for LAMP1-positive vesicles containing ApoE were 0.497 ± 0.090 for E4 and 0.410 ± 0.049 for E3. Differential receptor retention remains unresolved.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE isoform differences were manifested in the differential levels of internalized lipApoE (ApoE4 > ApoE3 > ApoE2), giving rise to the same isoform trend for LAMP1-positive vesicles containing ApoE immunoreactivity (Mander’s coefficients = 0.266 ± 0.045 for ApoE2, 0.410 ± 0.049 for ApoE3, 0.497 ± 0.090 for ApoE4) (Figure 2I).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (more internalized ApoE and more ApoE-containing lysosomal compartments)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE-knockout iPSC-derived astrocytes from ThermoFisher A18945; 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE for one day; ApoE/LDLR/LAMP1 imaging, internalized ApoE quantification and Mander’s overlap analysis.

rows.Finding description: Simultaneous ApoE3 or ApoE4 treatment inhibited LDL uptake by 60–65%, consistent with shared LDLR competition; the text does not assign separate effects to the two isoforms.
rows.Finding quote: When cells were co-treated with lipApoE and DiI-LDL for 3–4 h, both lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 led to 60–65% inhibition of DiI-LDL uptake, likely via a direct competition with LDL for LDLR binding, whereas lipApoE2 had no effect (Figure 2J, L).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (shared inhibition of LDL uptake; additional E4 effect unresolved)
rows.Experimental system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells serum-starved for 1.5–2 h; simultaneous 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated ApoE and 10 μg/mL DiI-LDL for 3–4 h; live confocal imaging.
rows.Data location: Fig 2J (co-treatment images) and Fig 2L (co-treatment quantification), with 60–65% reported in the associated Results

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.

rows.Finding description: Across nine biological replicates from three independent experiments, apoE4 reduced sortilin recycling by 50% relative to apoE3 in the CHO-cell biotinylation assay.
rows.Finding quote: In these studies, the amount of receptors recycling back to the cell surface was reduced by 50% in apoE4-treated as com- pared to apoE3-treated cells (Figures 6D, E
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (reduced sortilin recycling to the cell surface)
rows.Experimental system: Hamster CHO-S cells expressing murine sortilin; surface-biotinylation assay with 5 µg/mL apoE3 or apoE4, 15-minute internalization and 60-minute recycling at 37 °C, dynasore treatment, and glutathione stripping. Recycling was calculated from the loss of intracellular biotinylated sortilin measured by western blot densitometry; nine biological replicates from three independent experiments.

rows.Finding description: Antibody-labeled sortilin returned to the CHO-cell surface with apoE3, whereas apoE4 caused internalized receptors to remain largely intracellular during the recycling assay.
rows.Finding quote: The recycling path of sortilin established in CHO cells was not impacted by the presence of apoE3 in the culture medium (Figure 6B). However, in the presence of apoE4, internalized receptors failed to re-appear on the cell surface and remained largely intracellular (Fig- ure 6B
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (reduced cell-surface recycling and increased intracellular retention of sortilin)
rows.Experimental system: Hamster CHO-S cells stably expressing murine sortilin in apoE3- or apoE4-conditioned medium; surface receptors antibody-labeled at 4 °C, internalized for 15 minutes at 37 °C, then assessed after 60 minutes with dynasore at 37 °C. Immunostaining of permeabilized versus non-permeabilized cells distinguished total and surface receptor pools.

rows.Finding description: In 15–18 CHO cells per condition, the thresholded Manders tM1 analysis showed significantly greater colocalization of sortilin–apoE complexes with transferrin under apoE4 than apoE3 treatment.
rows.Finding quote: Colocalization of receptor/ligand complexes in Tf-positive cell compartments was significantly higher in apoE4 as compared with apoE3 treated cells as shown by Manders’ values tM1 (C) and tM2 (D).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (higher Manders tM1 colocalization of sortilin–apoE complexes with transferrin)
rows.Experimental system: Hamster CHO-S cells expressing murine sortilin; 2-hour treatment with 5 µg/mL myc-tagged apoE3 or apoE4 followed by 20 minutes with 25 µg/mL fluorescent transferrin; thresholded Manders tM1 analysis of PLA and transferrin signals. The legend reports 15–18 cells per condition in replicate experiments.

rows.Finding description: Representative CHO-cell images showed greater localization of sortilin–apoE4 complexes than sortilin–apoE3 complexes in transferrin-positive early endocytic or recycling compartments.
rows.Finding quote: The extent of co-localization of sortilin/apoE complexes (PLA signal) with Tf was significantly higher with apoE4 as compared with apoE3 (Figure 5C, D).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater sortilin–apoE complex localization in transferrin-positive endocytic/recycling compartments)
rows.Experimental system: Hamster CHO-S cells stably expressing murine sortilin, treated for 2 hours with 5 µg/mL myc-tagged apoE3 or apoE4, followed by 25 µg/mL Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated transferrin for another 20 minutes; proximity ligation and fluorescence imaging. No human brain cells were tested.
rows.Data location: Fig 5B; representative images quantified in Fig 5C and Fig 5D

rows.Finding description: After 24 hours of apoE exposure, sortilin–apoE3 complexes were dispersed throughout CHO-cell cytoplasm, whereas sortilin–apoE4 complexes showed a juxtamembrane pattern consistent with altered trafficking.
rows.Finding quote: Co-localization of sortilin with apoE3 was seen in a scattered vesicular pattern throughout the cytoplasm, whereas co-localization with apoE4 showed a distinct pattern close to the cell membrane (Figure 5A).
rows.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (juxtamembrane rather than dispersed cytoplasmic localization of sortilin–apoE complexes)
rows.Experimental system: Chinese hamster ovary cells stably expressing murine sortilin (CHO-S), treated for 24 hours at 37 °C with 5 µg/mL myc-tagged apoE3 or apoE4 produced in HEK293 cells; proximity ligation assay using anti-sortilin and anti-myc antibodies. These were hamster cells, not human brain cells.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes impaired ARF6-related recycling of receptors between the cell surface and the endosome, compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: HPTLC analysis of secreted cholesterol, cholesteryl esters (CE), and phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) in APOE-isogenic human iAstrocytes showed significantly lower cholesterol and CE secretion in APOE4 than APOE3, providing an indirect ABCA1-function surrogate.
rows.Finding quote: Interestingly, secreted cholesterol and CE were significantly decreased only in APOE4 iAstrocytes (Figures S2A and S2B).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower cholesterol and CE secretion in human iAstrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human quiescent iPSC-derived astrocytes from EBiSC CRISPR-generated APOE-isogenic lines BIONi010-C-2 (APOE3) and BIONi010-C-4 (APOE4), each expressing a single APOE allele; differentiated through neural progenitor cells using a 44-day astrocyte differentiation protocol; baseline without cytokine stimulation; secreted lipids measured by HPTLC and normalized to cellular phosphatidylcholine.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, flow cytometry showed a lower baseline Aβ42 uptake trend in APOE4 versus APOE3 human isogenic iAstrocytes with no significant difference (p = 0.054), while RAP significantly decreased uptake in APOE3 but caused no significant difference in APOE4 (p = 0.23).
rows.Finding quote: A flow-cytometry-based Aβ42 uptake assay, using pre-aggregated Hilyte488-tagged Aβ42, showed an allele-dependent trend in uptake capacity (KO > E2 > E3 ≥ E4), although differences between APOE3 and APOE4 did not reach significance (p = 0.054) (Figure 2F). Interestingly, APOE-KO cells showed the highest Aβ42 uptake capacity. Aβ42 is mostly taken up through receptor-dependent endocytosis, such as LRP1. To determine if Aβ uptake in iAstrocytes is mediated by LDLR-dependent endocytosis, we treated cells with a low concentration of LDLR family antagonist receptor-associated protein (RAP), which primarily blocked LRP1 and very-low-density lipoprotein receptor (VLDLR), in order to induce a mild reduction in Aβ uptake, resulting in a measurable difference between genotypes. Blocking LDLR family members caused a significant decrease in Aβ uptake in APOE-KO, E2, and E3, but not in E4 iAstrocytes (p = 0.23).
rows.Finding summary: Baseline uptake trended lower in APOE4 than APOE3 (p = 0.054). RAP significantly reduced uptake in APOE3. Its effect in APOE4 did not reach significance (p = 0.23). The paper gives no genotype-by-RAP interaction test.
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE-isogenic iAstrocytes assayed by flow cytometry for the percentage of live Aβ-positive cells using 1 μM pre-aggregated labeled Aβ42, with or without 24 h pretreatment with 0.2 μM RAP. The supplied text does not verify two-hour Aβ exposure or continued RAP during exposure.

rows.Finding description: Across three independent experiments comparing glutamate uptake over 1 hour in APOE-isogenic human iAstrocytes, APOE4 cells showed lower uptake than APOE3 and the lowest uptake overall, providing an indirect functional surrogate for transporter availability without measuring ARF6-related recycling.
rows.Finding quote: Uptake of glutamate in iAstrocytes demonstrated an allele-dependent effect, with APOE4 iAstrocytes taking up the lowest amount of glutamate while APOE2 and APOE-KO took up the highest amounts (Figure 2D).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower glutamate uptake in human iAstrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human monoallelic EBiSC APOE3 and APOE4 iAstrocytes differentiated through day 44 and plated 24 h before assay. Glutamate uptake over 1 h was normalized to total lysate protein. The supplied text does not specify glutamine deprivation, glutamate concentration, assay temperature, or detection reagent.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes impaired ARF6-related recycling of receptors between the cell surface and the endosome, compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: After 1 day of treatment with lipidated ApoE, APOE-knockout human iPSC-derived astrocytes showed more internalized LDLR-associated ApoE and greater overlap of LAMP1-positive vesicles with ApoE for ApoE4 than ApoE3 (Mander’s coefficients 0.497 ± 0.090 versus 0.410 ± 0.049), indicating greater endolysosomal accumulation rather than directly measuring receptor recycling or ARF6 activity.
rows.Finding quote: ApoE isoform differences were manifested in the differential levels of internalized lipApoE (ApoE4 > ApoE3 > ApoE2), giving rise to the same isoform trend for LAMP1-positive vesicles containing ApoE immunoreactivity (Mander’s coefficients = 0.266 ± 0.045 for ApoE2, 0.410 ± 0.049 for ApoE3, 0.497 ± 0.090 for ApoE4) (Figure 2I).
rows.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4) -> (greater internalized LDLR-associated ApoE and ApoE accumulation in LAMP1-positive compartments in human iPSC-derived astrocytes)
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE-knockout iPSC-derived astrocytes generated by CRISPR/Cas9 editing of ThermoFisher A18945 iPSCs, originally APOE3 homozygous; treated for 1 day with 10 μg/mL HEK293-derived, POPC-lipidated human ApoE3 or ApoE4; fixed-cell ApoE, endogenous LDLR and LAMP1 immunostaining, super-resolution confocal imaging, and ImageJ Coloc2 Mander’s overlap analysis.

rows.Finding description: After 1 day of lipidated ApoE4 treatment, super-resolution imaging of human APOE KO iPSC-derived astrocytes showed complete colocalization of internalized ApoE4 with endogenous LDLR (Mander’s coefficient = 1), predominantly within LAMP1-positive compartments (Mander’s coefficient = 0.900 ± 0.008), supporting receptor trapping without establishing greater recycling impairment than ApoE3.
rows.Finding quote: Super-resolution imaging on APOE KO iAstrocytes confirmed internalized lipApoE completely colocalized with endogenous LDLR (Mander’s coefficient for ApoE puncta with colocalizing LDLR = 1 for all 3 isoforms), largely inside LAMP1 compartments (Figure 2H) (Mander’s coefficients for ApoE puncta with colocalizing LAMP1 = 0.823 ± 0.061 for ApoE2; 0.903 ± 0.024 for ApoE3; 0.900 ± 0.008 for ApoE4).
rows.Finding summary: The fraction of internalized ApoE overlapping LDLR was identical for all three isoforms. The fractions overlapping LAMP1 were numerically similar for ApoE3 and ApoE4. Recycling rates were unmeasured.
rows.Experimental system: Human APOE knockout iPSC-derived astrocytes generated from CRISPR/Cas9-edited ThermoFisher A18945 iPSCs, originally APOE3 homozygous; treated with 10 μg/mL POPC-lipidated, HEK293-derived human ApoE4 for 1 day; fixed-cell super-resolution confocal co-immunostaining of ApoE, endogenous LDLR, and LAMP1, with ImageJ Coloc2 Mander’s overlap analysis; exact astrocyte age at assay not stated.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Across the sampled ages, APPPS1:E4 and APPPS1:E3 mice showed no significant genotype main effect on apoE levels in the insoluble, guanidine-extracted whole-hemibrain fraction.
rows.Finding quote: We measured apolipoprotein levels in the guanidine hydrochloride-soluble brain fractions. APPPS1:E4 mice exhibited a main effect of age (p = 0.0003), with 16-month-old mice displaying significantly higher levels of apoE than the two younger age groups (Figure 4S). There was no main effect of the APOE allele when evaluating both the APPPS1:E3 and APPPS1:E4 mice (Figure 4T, p = 0.2003).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in insoluble whole-hemibrain apoE levels)
rows.Experimental system: Whole hemibrains from eight-, 12-, and 16-month-old APPswe/PS1dE9 heterozygous mice homozygous for human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted replacement, C57BL/6 background; sexes pooled; Tper-insoluble material extracted with guanidine hydrochloride and apoE measured using HJ15.6 capture and HJ15.4b detection antibodies; 3-11 mice/group; no subcellular localization.
rows.Data location: Fig 4T, genotype main effect across ages

rows.Finding description: At 12 months, insoluble whole-hemibrain apoE levels appeared higher in APPPS1:E4 mice than APPPS1:E3 mice, but there was no significant difference.
rows.Finding quote: Mice with the APOE4 allele appeared to have higher apoE levels at 12 and 16 months, but the difference was insignificant.
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in insoluble whole-hemibrain apoE levels at 12 months)
rows.Experimental system: Whole hemibrains from 12-month-old APPswe/PS1dE9 heterozygous mice homozygous for human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted replacement, C57BL/6 background; sexes pooled; Tper-insoluble material extracted with guanidine hydrochloride and apoE measured using HJ15.6 capture and HJ15.4b detection antibodies; legend reports 3-11 mice/group across this panel; no subcellular localization.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 undergoes increased aggregation in the endo-lysosome compared with APOE3.

rows.Finding description: Western blotting of anterior cingulate cortex detergent-solubilized pellets from two human siblings, one APOE4 homozygote and one APOE3 homozygote, showed more high-molecular-weight apoE-containing complexes and apoE fragments in the APOE4 sibling.
rows.Finding quote: However, apoE fragments and larger complexes in ACC were more abundant in Patient 1 (Figure 2F).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4) -> (more high-molecular-weight apoE-containing complexes in anterior cingulate cortex)
rows.Experimental system: Postmortem human anterior cingulate cortex from two siblings with C9ORF72 repeat expansions and familial FTLD-MND, one APOE ε4/ε4 and one APOE ε3/ε3. Reported ages at death were 61 and 60 years, respectively; demographic information was modified for privacy. Postmortem collection intervals were 12.8 and 6.5 hours, respectively. Detergent-solubilized pellet fractions were analyzed by SDS–PAGE and anti-human apoE western blotting, with 10 μg protein per lane. No cell-type or endosomal/lysosomal localization was measured.

hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.

rows.Finding description: In cultured mouse pericytes, proximity ligation showed barely detectable APOE4–LRP1 association compared with APOE3–LRP1 association in six experiments, providing a binding-strength surrogate without measuring receptor recycling.
rows.Finding quote: By imaging APOE/LRP1 proximity ligation in pericytes we demonstrated that APOE3 (Fig. 4b) and murine Apoe (not shown) bind with high affinity to LRP1, whereas the APOE4–LRP1 interaction was barely detectable (Fig. 4b).
rows.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower apoE–LRP1 association in pericytes)
rows.Experimental system: Cultured mouse pericytes exposed to astrocyte-derived human APOE3 or APOE4; APOE–LRP1 proximity ligation imaging. The associated culture experiments use Apoe−/− pericytes, and mouse lines were maintained on a C57Bl6 background. Donor age and exposure duration are not specified for this panel. Human brain cells, binding kinetics, endosomal dissociation, and receptor recycling were not measured.
